title: INSTALL PRESSURE PLATE / PERFORMANCE TEST OF COMPRESSOR

content.description: Close-up view of pressure plate component being installed on compressor

items: (a) Adjust the clearance between the pressure plate and rotor by placing shims on the compressor shaft.

content.text: If the clearance is not within tolerance, add or reduce the number of shims to obtain the standard clearance.

content.description: Compressor assembly showing SST tool installation location

items: (b) Using SST and a torque wrench, install the shaft nut.

content.description: Test setup showing compressor connected to pressure gauge reading 3 kg/cm² with cap and service valve connections

items: (a) Put caps on both service valves.
(b) Charge the compressor with refrigerant through the charging valve until the pressure is 3 kg/cm² (43 psi, 294 kPa).
(c) Using a gas leak detector, check the compressor for leaks.

content.text: If leaks are found, check and replace the gasket, O ring, or shaft seal.
2. IF NECESSARY FILL COMPRESSOR WITH CLEAN COMPRESSOR OIL
Remove the service valve and drain the compressor oil. Fill with new oil.
Compressor oil: DENSOIL 6, SUNISO No. 5GS or equivalent
3. EVACUATE COMPRESSOR AND CHARGE WITH REFRIGERANT (See page AC-12)
Make sure the caps are tight and free from moisture and contamination.
NOTE: When storing a compressor for an extended period, charge it with refrigerant or dry nitrogen gas to prevent corrosion.
